children: Moldova's central bank on Thursday hiked its key interest rate to 9% from 7.5%, the third increase this year, as it works to counter rising inflation.

"The decision by the National Bank of Moldova to maintain a restrictive monetary policy was taken against a backdrop of increasing inflationary pressures," the regulator's press service said in a statement.
It cited unfavourable trends in international prices for energy, food and raw materials, and from the domestic demand side, supported by the dynamic of household disposable income.
In August, the bank raised the rate by 0.5% to 7.5%.
Moldova's annual consumer price inflation reached 6.96% in August, the National Bureau of Statistics said last week.
Moldova's central bank sees annual inflation at 7.2% this year, after it hit 6.8% in 2025.
